rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: CUDA uses warps to let 32 threads share instruction scheduling while processing different data, which supports high throughput. Divergent branches can reduce efficiency because different paths execute with only the relevant threads active, leaving other lanes idle. Consecutive memory accesses help because the GPU can combine those accesses into fewer memory transactions.

rows.name: spoken-why-during-coding-frozen-21
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: A circular array gives the FIFO exactly 17 usable slots without allocating memory during push or pop, and both operations take constant time. Tracking the head and the number of stored items distinguishes empty from full, so a push can reject overflow without overwriting unread data. Advancing indices modulo 17 preserves FIFO order through wraparound, which the tests should explicitly verify.

rows.name: saved-audio-23-frozen-30
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because “unreliable” describes the customer’s experience, not the cause, and different failures need different fixes. Tracing affected orders and comparing promised with actual outcomes helps identify where the service breaks down rather than treating the loudest complaint as the whole problem. Prioritizing safety and essential-supply risks first, then the biggest recurring failure, directs effort toward the greatest customer harm and gives us a measurable way to check whether the fix works.
